scenario: 面试官让你解释你如何驱动 AI agent 完成工程任务，而不是只问你用过哪些工具。
scenario_en: The interviewer wants you to explain how you drive an AI agent through engineering work, not just list which tools you've used.
q: 面试官问「你怎么用 AI/agent 工作」，最能拿分的回答核心是什么？
q_en: The interviewer asks how you work with AI/agents — what's the strongest core answer?
options: 把用过的 AI 工具按项目顺序逐一报一遍，讲清版本和特性
强调自己几乎全程手写代码，尽量少让 AI 插手关键逻辑
把 agent 当成要工程化驾驭的系统：讲清怎么喂上下文、定成功标准、防失败
强调 AI 很快会取代程序员，讨论这份工作还有没有必要存在
options_en: List every AI tool you've used, project by project, with versions and features.
Emphasize that you hand-write almost all the code and rarely let AI touch core logic.
Treat the agent as a system to engineer: how you feed context, define success, and guard against failure.
Emphasize that AI will soon replace programmers and question whether the job still matters.
why: 这题考工程化理解，不是工具清单：高分答案讲清怎么喂上下文、怎么定义成功(evals)、怎么防失败(failure modes)。
why_en: The strongest answer treats the agent as an engineered system: how you feed context, define success with evals, and prevent failure modes.
whenOtherWins: 如果问题明确是工具经验盘点，可以简短列工具，但仍要回到你如何控制质量和风险。
tradeoff: 工具清单的广度 vs 工程化驾驭的深度

termDefinitions.meaning: 人工智能，这里指驱动 agent 决策和生成代码的大模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AI here means the large language model that powers the agent's decisions and code generation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 能自主感知环境、规划步骤、调用工具完成任务的程序系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An agent is a program that autonomously perceives its environment, plans steps, and calls tools to complete a task.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用来衡量 agent 产出是否达标的量化评估方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Evals are the quantitative methods used to measure whether an agent's output meets the bar.

termDefinitions.meaning: agent 系统性会出错的方式，比如幻觉、跑偏、死循环。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Failure modes are the systematic ways an agent can go wrong, such as hallucination, scope creep, or infinite loops.

optionMeanings: 把评估简化为工具使用清单
把评估简化为纯手写编码能力
把 agent 定义为需要工程化驾驭的系统
把话题带向 AI 替代程序员的争论
optionMeanings_en: Reduces the answer to a list of tools used.
Reduces the answer to pure hand-written coding skill.
Frames the agent as a system that needs to be engineered.
Steers the topic toward AI replacing programmers.
optionScenarioImpacts: 面试官听到的只是名词罗列，看不出你的判断力
容易显得你不了解如何有效借助 AI 提效
面试官能看到你怎么控制上下文、成功标准和失败模式
偏离了「你怎么用 agent 工作」这个具体问题
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The interviewer hears a list of names and sees no judgment.
It can make you look unable to use AI effectively.
The interviewer sees how you control context, success criteria, and failure modes.
It drifts away from the actual question of how you work with an agent.
optionDirectness: 只有被追问「你用过哪些工具」时才该切到这个角度
只有面试官明确要求「完全不用 AI」时才该强调这点
面试官问工作方式时，这个角度最贴合工程化判断
只有话题本身在讨论行业趋势时才适合展开这点
optionDirectness_en: Fits only when the interviewer separately asks which tools you've used.
Fits only if the interviewer explicitly asks about working without AI at all.
Fits best when the interviewer asks how you work — it matches engineering judgment.
Fits only when the topic itself is about industry trends.

scenario: 你要在白板上画出一个自主 agent 从接到任务到完成的完整运行链路。
scenario_en: You're sketching on a whiteboard how an autonomous agent runs end-to-end, from receiving a task to finishing it.
q: 一个自主 agent 的基本工作循环是什么？
q_en: What is the basic working loop of an autonomous agent?
options: 读取上下文、规划下一步、调用工具行动、观察结果，再对照成功标准判断是否收尾
把最终代码方案一次性生成，不做任何验证或修正就交付
只生成代码草稿，从来不真正执行，也不做任何验证
不断随机尝试各种可能操作，直到偶然凑巧碰对答案
options_en: Read context, plan the next step, act via a tool, observe the result, then check it against success criteria before looping again.
Generate the final code solution in one shot and ship it with no verification or correction.
Only draft code but never actually execute it or verify anything.
Keep randomly trying possible actions until one happens to work by luck.
why: agent = 在循环里运行的 LLM。工程发力点都在这个循环的每一步：上下文、工具、验证、终止条件。
why_en: An agent is an LLM in a loop: read context, plan, act via tools, observe, then verify against success criteria before looping again.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  P[读取上下文] --> PL[规划下一步]
  PL --> A[调用工具 行动]
  A --> O[观察结果]
  O --> V{达到成功标准?}
  V -->|否| PL
  V -->|是| D[完成]

termDefinitions.meaning: 大语言模型，agent 循环里做规划和决策的核心引擎。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An LLM is the large language model that drives planning and decisions inside the agent loop.

termDefinitions.meaning: 能自主感知环境、规划步骤、调用工具完成任务的程序系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An agent is a program that autonomously perceives its environment, plans steps, and calls tools to complete a task.

optionMeanings: 把 agent 定义为「读取-规划-行动-观察-验证」的循环
把 agent 等同于一次性生成器，没有中间验证
把 agent 等同于只写代码、不执行的草稿机
把 agent 等同于无方向的随机尝试
optionMeanings_en: Defines an agent as a read-plan-act-observe-verify loop.
Equates the agent with a one-shot generator that has no verification step.
Equates the agent with a draft generator that never executes.
Equates the agent with directionless random trial and error.
optionScenarioImpacts: 链路能完整解释每一步该加什么工程手段
画出的链路会少掉观察和纠错，无法解释怎么处理错误
链路缺了行动和观察，说明不了 agent 怎么真正干活
链路没有规划和终止条件，解释不了成功标准怎么起作用
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The chain fully explains what engineering lever belongs at each step.
The chain drawn is missing observation and correction, so it can't explain error handling.
The chain is missing action and observation, so it can't explain how the agent actually works.
The chain has no planning or stop condition, so it can't explain how success criteria matter.
optionDirectness: 描述通用自主 agent 循环时最贴切
只有极简单、不需要迭代的任务才可能一次成型
只适合纯生成、不需要执行反馈的辅助场景
几乎不适用于任何工程场景，缺少收敛机制
optionDirectness_en: Fits best when describing the general autonomous-agent loop.
Fits only extremely simple tasks that never need iteration.
Fits only pure-generation assistance that never needs execution feedback.
Fits almost no engineering scenario since it has no convergence mechanism.

scenario: 你要决定把一个任务做成固定 workflow，还是让模型自主规划、调用工具并迭代。
scenario_en: You must decide whether to build a task as a fixed workflow or let the model plan, call tools, and iterate on its own.
q: 该先用固定 workflow，还是该上能自主决策的 agent？
q_en: Should you use a fixed workflow, or an agent that decides autonomously?
options: 只要能用 agent 就用，它永远比固定 workflow 更好用
agent 不需要任何工具，也能独立完成整个工程任务
两者本质上没有区别，选哪个都不影响结果
复杂、高价值、模型能胜任、出错可恢复时才上 agent，否则用固定 workflow
options_en: Use an agent whenever you can — it's always better than a fixed workflow.
An agent can finish the whole engineering task without any tools at all.
The two are basically the same, so it doesn't matter which one you pick.
Only go agentic when the task is complex, high-value, the model can handle it, and errors are recoverable — otherwise use a fixed workflow.
why: 先用最简单的方案；workflow 是预定义路径，agent 让模型自决步骤。判断看四问：复杂度、价值、可行性、错误代价，任一为否就别上 agent。
why_en: Go agentic only when the task is complex, valuable, the model can handle it, and errors are recoverable — otherwise keep the predefined workflow.
whenOtherWins: 如果任务路径稳定、错误代价高，或规则就能覆盖，固定 workflow 更可控、更便宜。
tradeoff: agent 自主决策的灵活性 vs 固定 workflow 的可控与低成本

termDefinitions.meaning: 预定义的固定代码执行路径，步骤和顺序在写代码时就确定。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A workflow is a predefined code path where the steps and order are fixed at authoring time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 能自主感知环境、规划步骤、调用工具完成任务的程序系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An agent is a program that autonomously perceives its environment, plans steps, and calls tools to complete a task.

optionMeanings: 认为 agent 在任何场景都比 workflow 更优
认为 agent 完全不需要工具就能独立工作
认为两种方案没有区别、可以随便选
把上 agent 的决策浓缩成四个判断条件
optionMeanings_en: Assumes an agent beats a workflow in every scenario.
Assumes an agent can work independently with no tools at all.
Assumes the two approaches are equivalent and interchangeable.
Condenses the decision to go agentic into four concrete conditions.
optionScenarioImpacts: 会在简单任务上过度设计，白白增加不确定性和成本
忽视了 agent 本来就要靠工具行动这一核心机制
会让本该稳定可控的任务承担不必要的行为风险
能按复杂度、价值、可行性、错误代价四问做出取舍
optionScenarioImpacts_en: It over-engineers simple tasks, adding unneeded uncertainty and cost.
It ignores that acting through tools is the agent's core mechanism.
It exposes a task that should be stable and controllable to needless behavioral risk.
Lets you decide using four questions: complexity, value, feasibility, and error cost.
optionDirectness: 只有全部四个判断条件都成立时才对，不能无脑套用
只有纯推理、完全不需要外部行动的任务才成立
只有两个方案代价和可控性完全等价时才成立，现实很少见
四问都满足时最贴合「什么时候该上 agent」这个判断
optionDirectness_en: Only valid when all four conditions actually hold — never a blanket rule.
Fits only pure-reasoning tasks that never need any external action.
Only valid when cost and controllability are truly identical, which is rare in practice.
Fits best when all four questions point the same way — that's exactly when to go agentic.

scenario: 生产环境里，写码、测试、审查、安全四个专职 agent 排成流水线，由一个协调者按顺序派活。
scenario_en: In production, four specialized agents — coding, testing, review, and security — run in a pipeline, dispatched in order by one orchestrator.
q: 这种「协调者派活给专职子 agent」的结构属于哪种模式？
q_en: What pattern is this 'orchestrator delegates to specialized sub-agents' structure?
options: prompt chaining（提示链）
orchestrator-workers（编排器-子 agent）
autocomplete 自动补全
single-shot 单次 prompt 直出结果
options_en: Prompt chaining (a serial chain of prompts).
Orchestrator-workers (an orchestrator delegating to sub-agents).
Autocomplete.
A single-shot prompt that outputs a result directly.
why: 生产里常见「数字装配线」：编排器把活派给专职子 agent，靠 MCP 等协议打通工具，这是六大 agentic 模式之一。
why_en: A production pipeline like this has an orchestrator delegating to specialized sub-agents wired together via MCP — one of six agentic patterns.
tradeoff: 编排器统一派活的协作深度 vs 单个 agent 独立完成的简单性

rows: 串行步骤，前一步喂后一步
一个生成、一个评判迭代
模型自主决定轨迹和工具

termDefinitions.meaning: 让 agent 以统一协议连接外部工具和数据源的标准。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MCP is a standard protocol that lets an agent connect to external tools and data sources uniformly.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个编排器把任务拆给多个专职子 agent 分别处理的架构模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Orchestrator-workers is a pattern where one orchestrator splits a task across specialized sub-agents.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把任务拆成串行步骤，前一步的输出作为后一步的输入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Prompt chaining breaks a task into serial steps, feeding each step's output into the next.

termDefinitions.meaning: 根据已有上下文补全下一段文本或代码，不具备多步自主规划。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Autocomplete predicts the next chunk of text or code from context, without multi-step autonomous planning.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次性把问题丢给模型，只产出一次直接结果，没有循环或分工。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A single-shot prompt asks the model once and gets one direct result, with no loop or division of labor.

optionMeanings: 把流水线结构误认成串行提示链
编排器统一派活，子 agent 各管一段
把多 agent 协作误认成简单文本补全
把整个流水线误认成一次性直出
optionMeanings_en: Mistakes the pipeline structure for a serial prompt chain.
One orchestrator dispatches work while sub-agents each own a slice.
Mistakes multi-agent collaboration for simple text completion.
Mistakes the whole pipeline for a single direct output.
optionScenarioImpacts: 看不出协调者独立派活给专职子 agent 这一层
准确对应写码测试审查安全四个专职角色分工
完全忽略了协调派活和多角色分工
忽略了四个阶段各自独立运行、有中间产出
optionScenarioImpacts_en: It misses the layer where one coordinator dispatches work to specialized sub-agents.
It matches exactly the four specialized roles: coding, testing, review, security.
It completely ignores the coordination and division of roles.
It ignores that the four stages run independently with intermediate outputs.
optionDirectness: 只有任务是严格线性接力、没有独立协调者时才对
有独立协调者+多个专职子 agent 时最贴合
只适用于单一模型补全下一段文本，没有多 agent 场景
只有任务能被压缩成一次调用时才成立，这里明显不是
optionDirectness_en: Fits only a strict linear relay with no independent coordinator.
Fits best when there's one coordinator plus several specialized sub-agents.
Fits only single-model text completion, with no multi-agent setup at all.
Fits only when the task collapses into one call, which clearly isn't the case here.

scenario: code agent 执行任务时，日志显示它调用了一个从未出现在工具列表里的函数名。
scenario_en: While running a task, a code agent's log shows it calling a function name that never appeared in its tool list.
q: 这属于下面哪一种失败模式？
q_en: Which failure mode does this describe?
options: 范围蔓延，在陌生环境里跑偏
提前终止，任务没做完就收尾
幻觉 / 编造动作
工具误用，传错了参数
options_en: Scope creep, drifting off track in an unfamiliar environment.
Premature termination, wrapping up before the task is done.
Hallucination / fabricated actions.
Tool misuse, passing the wrong parameters.
why: 编造一个不存在的工具/函数名并尝试调用，是「幻觉/编造动作」的典型样例——模型生成的是看似合理却不真实的输出。
why_en: Inventing a tool name that was never given and calling it anyway is a textbook hallucinated action — plausible-looking but unreal output.

rows: 调用不存在的工具或数据
没做完就收尾，或停不下来
明确可量化的完成标准
在陌生环境里越界操作
精确规格+阶段性校验门
参数传错或误调用工具
工具层护栏，参数校验/幂等
长任务里忘记早期约束
多阶段校验+人在环审批

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型生成看似合理但实际不存在或不真实的内容。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hallucination is when a model generates plausible-sounding output that is not actually real or true.

termDefinitions.meaning: agent 在执行中悄悄扩大了任务边界，触碰了不该动的部分。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Scope creep is when an agent quietly expands beyond the task's intended boundary.

termDefinitions.meaning: agent 调用工具时传错参数或用错工具，导致操作出错。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Tool misuse is when an agent calls a tool with the wrong parameters or the wrong tool entirely.

optionMeanings: agent 悄悄扩大了任务范围、动了不该动的东西
任务还没完成 agent 就提前收尾了
模型编造出实际不存在的工具/数据
调用了正确的工具，但参数传错了
optionMeanings_en: The agent quietly expands beyond the task and touches things it shouldn't.
The agent wraps up before the task is actually complete.
The model invents a tool or piece of data that never existed.
The correct tool is called, but with the wrong parameters.
optionScenarioImpacts: 跟「编造一个函数名」这个具体现象不吻合
日志现象是调用了错的函数，不是收尾过早
正好对应日志里那个从未注册过的函数名
这里的问题是函数本身就不存在，不是参数传错
optionScenarioImpacts_en: It doesn't match the specific symptom of inventing a function name.
The log shows a wrong function call, not an early wrap-up.
It matches exactly the never-registered function name in the log.
The problem here is the function doesn't exist at all, not a bad parameter.
optionDirectness: 只有 agent 真的越界操作了任务范围外的资源才对
只有任务半途而废、没达成目标才适用
看到模型调用了列表外的工具/函数时最贴切
只有工具本身存在、只是参数用错时才适用
optionDirectness_en: Fits only when the agent actually operates on resources outside the task's scope.
Fits only when the task is abandoned halfway without reaching its goal.
Fits best when the model calls a tool or function outside its given list.
Fits only when the tool itself exists and just the parameters are wrong.

scenario: 你的 code agent 有时停不下来一直烧钱，有时又没做完就收尾。
scenario_en: Your code agent sometimes runs forever burning cost, and other times stops before the task is actually done.
q: 该给 agent 补上什么，才能同时防死循环和防收尾过早？
q_en: What should you add to the agent to prevent both infinite loops and early stopping?
options: 定义明确可量化的完成标准，给循环清晰终止条件
换一个参数量更大、更贵的基础模型
干脆不给 agent 配任何外部工具
不断往 prompt 里堆更多形容词和提示词
options_en: Define explicit, measurable completion criteria that give the loop a clear stop condition.
Switch to a bigger, more expensive base model.
Simply give the agent no external tools at all.
Keep piling more adjectives and instructions into the prompt.
why: 明确的完成标准把无限循环变成告警而不是天价账单；像给探员写任务书一样定义可量化的成功条件。
why_en: Explicit completion criteria turn a runaway loop into an alert instead of a runaway bill, by giving the agent a quantifiable definition of done.
whenOtherWins: 如果任务本来就简单、几步就能完事，加终止条件的工程成本可能不值得。
tradeoff: 可量化终止条件的确定性 vs 模型/工具/提示词调整的间接性

termDefinitions.meaning: 喂给模型的指令文本，用来设定任务和期望输出。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A prompt is the instruction text given to a model to set the task and expected output.

termDefinitions.meaning: 判断任务是否算完成的可量化条件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Completion criteria are the quantifiable conditions that determine whether a task counts as done.

optionMeanings: 给循环补上可量化的完成/终止条件
把问题误归因到模型能力不足
把问题误归因到工具太多
把问题误归因到提示词不够多
optionMeanings_en: Adds a quantifiable completion condition that stops the loop.
Misattributes the problem to insufficient model capability.
Misattributes the problem to having too many tools.
Misattributes the problem to not having enough prompt text.
optionScenarioImpacts: 同时防住死循环烧钱和收尾过早两种情况
换模型不会给循环加终止条件，问题依旧
没工具 agent 更难完成任务，无法解决终止问题
堆词不会给循环一个可量化的停止信号
optionScenarioImpacts_en: It guards against both a runaway loop and stopping too early.
Swapping models doesn't add a stop condition — the problem remains.
Without tools the agent struggles even more and the stop problem is unsolved.
Piling on words gives the loop no quantifiable stop signal.
optionDirectness: 循环没有清晰终止条件时最贴切
只有真正因为模型能力不足才答错时才适用
只有工具本身在制造无限循环时才沾边
只有提示词本身缺失必要信息时才有点用
optionDirectness_en: Fits best when the loop has no clear stop condition.
Fits only when the model's capability is genuinely the bottleneck.
Relevant only if the tools themselves are what's causing the infinite loop.
Only helps if the prompt is genuinely missing necessary information.

scenario: agent 的输出经常格式不对或编造字段，下游系统直接崩。
scenario_en: The agent's output is often malformed or has invented fields, and it crashes the downstream system.
q: 性价比最高的一道防线是什么？
q_en: What's the highest-ROI defense to add here?
options: 安排人工逐条检查所有输出
一旦报错就整体重启 agent 重来
忽略这个问题，反正大多数输出是对的
用 schema 校验输出格式，在进入下游前挡掉不合规内容
options_en: Have a human manually review every single output.
Restart the whole agent from scratch every time it errors.
Ignore the problem since most outputs are correct anyway.
Validate output against a schema and block noncompliant results before they hit downstream systems.
why: schema 校验是最高 ROI 的韧性手段之一：结构化输出符合机器可校验的格式，低成本挡掉大量幻觉/畸形输出。
why_en: Schema validation is one of the highest-ROI resilience patterns — machine-checkable structured output cheaply catches malformed or hallucinated results.
whenOtherWins: 如果输出格式本来就自由（如长文创作），schema 校验意义不大，更适合靠人工或 LLM judge 把关。
tradeoff: 机器可校验的低成本防线 vs 人工逐条检查的高成本保障

termDefinitions.meaning: 描述数据应有字段和类型的规范，用来机器校验输出是否合规。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A schema defines the expected fields and types of data, letting a machine check whether output is valid.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型按预定义格式(如 JSON schema)产出结果，而不是自由文本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Structured output means the model produces results in a predefined format, such as JSON matching a schema, instead of free text.

optionMeanings: 靠人力逐条兜底校验
出错就整体重启，没有针对性校验
放任不管，赌大多数输出没问题
用机器可校验的格式规则挡在下游前面
optionMeanings_en: Relies on a human to check every item as a backstop.
Restarts everything on any error, with no targeted validation.
Does nothing and bets that most outputs are fine.
Uses a machine-checkable format rule as a gate before downstream systems.
optionScenarioImpacts: 能挡住错误，但人力成本随输出量线性增长
浪费已完成的工作，也不保证下次不再出错
少数错误一旦流入下游系统仍会崩溃
低成本挡住大量幻觉和畸形输出，规模化可行
optionScenarioImpacts_en: It catches errors, but labor cost grows linearly with output volume.
It wastes completed work and doesn't guarantee the next run avoids the error.
Even a few bad outputs reaching downstream systems still cause a crash.
It cheaply blocks most hallucinated or malformed output and scales well.
optionDirectness: 只有输出量很小、可以负担人工时才现实
只有重启成本极低、且错误随机不复现时才勉强适用
只有下游对错误完全容忍时才可能适用，通常不成立
输出量大、需要自动化把关时最贴切
optionDirectness_en: Realistic only when output volume is small enough for a human to keep up.
Barely works only when restarts are nearly free and errors are random, not systematic.
Only viable if downstream is fully tolerant of errors, which is rarely true.
Fits best when output volume is high and gating needs to be automated.

scenario: agent 感知不到你的代码库现状、运行环境和你的真实意图。
scenario_en: The agent can't perceive the current state of your codebase, its runtime environment, or your real intent.
q: 为了让它对齐，你要承担的核心工程任务是什么？
q_en: What's the core engineering task this creates, so the agent stays aligned?
options: 什么都不用管，相信模型自己能补全所有背景信息
做上下文工程：策划系统提示、精简工具、按需检索，给出精确规格和意图
把整个代码库一次性全部塞进上下文窗口喂给它
换成价格更贵、参数量更大的基础模型
options_en: Do nothing and trust the model to fill in all the missing background itself.
Do context engineering: curate the system prompt, trim tools, retrieve just-in-time, and give a precise spec and intent.
Dump the entire codebase into the context window all at once.
Switch to a more expensive base model with more parameters.
why: 上下文是有限资源，越长模型越容易走神(context rot)。要主动 curate：合适高度的提示、按需检索、必要时压缩。
why_en: Context is a finite resource — the longer it gets, the more the model drifts (context rot) — so you curate it deliberately instead of dumping everything in.

termDefinitions.meaning: 上下文越长，模型准确率和专注度反而下降的现象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Context rot is the phenomenon where a longer context window makes the model less accurate and less focused, not more.

termDefinitions.meaning: 为 agent 主动策划提示、工具、检索和记忆，而不是被动塞入所有信息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Context engineering is deliberately curating an agent's prompt, tools, retrieval, and memory instead of passively dumping in everything.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只在需要时才取相关信息，而不是提前把所有数据都放进上下文。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Just-in-time retrieval fetches only the information needed at the moment, instead of loading everything into context upfront.

optionMeanings: 假设模型能凭空补全缺失的项目背景
主动为 agent 策划提示、工具、检索和压缩
把全部代码库不加筛选地塞进上下文
把问题误归因为模型参数不够大
optionMeanings_en: Assumes the model can conjure up missing project background on its own.
Proactively curates the agent's prompt, tools, retrieval, and compaction.
Stuffs the entire codebase into context without any curation.
Misattributes the problem to the model not being large enough.
optionScenarioImpacts: 模型会猜测代码库状态，输出经常文不对题
让 agent 拿到刚好够用、准确的背景信息
触发 context rot，模型反而更容易走神出错
换模型不会补上它本来就拿不到的项目背景
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The model guesses at the codebase state and output often misses the mark.
The agent gets background information that is accurate and just enough.
It triggers context rot, making the model more likely to drift and err.
Swapping models doesn't supply the project background it never had access to.
optionDirectness: 只有任务极简单、不依赖具体环境时才勉强成立
感知不到环境和意图这个约束下最贴切
只有代码库极小、完全装得下时才可能不出问题
只有原模型确实能力不足时才是正确方向
optionDirectness_en: Barely holds only for extremely simple tasks that don't depend on the environment.
Fits best given the constraint that the agent can't perceive environment or intent on its own.
Only safe when the codebase is tiny enough to fit entirely.
Only the right move when the original model's capability is genuinely the bottleneck.

scenario: 你在给一个处理退款的 agent 写评估脚本，要决定主要给什么打分。
scenario_en: You're writing an eval script for a refund-processing agent and deciding what to grade primarily.
q: 评估 agent 时，应该主要给什么打分？
q_en: When evaluating an agent, what should you primarily grade?
options: 严格规定并检查它走的每一步操作路径
它一共调用了多少次工具、耗费多少 token
它最终达成的结果状态，路径(trajectory)只用来调试
它的回复措辞是否得体、风格是否讨喜
options_en: Strictly define and check every step of the path it takes.
How many tool calls it made and how many tokens it burned.
The final outcome it achieves — use the trajectory only to debug why.
Whether its wording is polite and its tone is likeable.
why: outcome(如「退款真落库了吗」)是客观达成证据；trajectory 只用来调试为什么。原则是主要给结果打分，别过度规定路径。
why_en: Grade the outcome, the final state such as whether the refund landed, and use the trajectory only to debug why it happened.
whenOtherWins: 如果需要审计安全合规或调试反复失败的用例，trajectory 检查同样必不可少。
tradeoff: 结果导向的评分客观性 vs 路径规定的可解释性/可调试性

rows: 判断任务是否真的完成
调试为什么失败或低效

termDefinitions.meaning: 任务执行后达成的最终状态，是否客观完成目标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Outcome is the final state after execution — whether the goal was objectively achieved.

termDefinitions.meaning: agent 为完成任务走过的具体步骤、工具调用和推理过程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Trajectory is the specific sequence of steps, tool calls, and reasoning an agent takes to complete a task.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型处理文本的最小计量单位，调用成本通常按 token 计费。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A token is the basic unit of text a model processes, and usage cost is typically billed per token.

optionMeanings: 把路径本身当成评分标准
把资源消耗量当成评分标准
把最终达成状态当成评分标准，路径只做调试
把语言风格当成评分标准
optionMeanings_en: Treats the path itself as the scoring criterion.
Treats resource consumption as the scoring criterion.
Treats the final achieved state as the score, using the path only for debugging.
Treats language style as the scoring criterion.
optionScenarioImpacts: 会惩罚 agent 找到的、你没预料到的有效解法
调用次数和 token 量说明不了任务是否真的完成
既不束缚 agent 找新解法，又能在失败时回查原因
退款有没有真正落库，跟措辞讨不讨喜无关
optionScenarioImpacts_en: It penalizes valid solutions the agent finds that you didn't anticipate.
Call count and token usage don't tell you whether the task was actually completed.
It doesn't constrain the agent's creativity yet still lets you trace failures.
Whether the refund actually landed has nothing to do with how likeable the wording is.
optionDirectness: 只有路径本身有强合规要求(如审计)时才该这样评
只有优化成本本身是目标时才该主要看这个
评估「任务是否真的完成」这个目标时最贴切
只有面向用户的语气确实是评估目标时才适用
optionDirectness_en: Should be graded this way only when the path itself has strict compliance requirements.
Worth grading mainly on this only when cost optimization itself is the goal.
Fits best when the goal is judging whether the task was truly completed.
Applies only when user-facing tone is itself the thing being evaluated.

scenario: 你要给一个多步骤 agent 建评估集，需要选合适的打分方式组合。
scenario_en: You're building an eval set for a multi-step agent and need to pick the right mix of graders.
q: code / LLM-judge / human 三种评分器该怎么组合使用？
q_en: How should you combine code-based, LLM-judge, and human graders?
options: code 查客观结果，LLM judge 打主观维度，定期人工校准
只用人工评分最稳妥、别的都不需要
只用 LLM 打分，不需要代码检查或人工介入
评分标准不重要，随便打个分数就行
options_en: Code checks objective outcomes, LLM-judge grades subjective dimensions, humans calibrate periodically.
Only use human review — nothing else is needed.
Only use an LLM to score — no code checks or human review needed.
The grading rubric doesn't matter much — any rough score works.
why: 有效评估通常组合：确定性 code 检查客观结果 + LLM rubric 打主观维度 + 定期人工校准，评估集从真实失败里攒。
why_en: Effective evals combine deterministic code checks for objective outcomes, an LLM rubric for subjective dimensions, and periodic human calibration.
whenOtherWins: 如果任务极简单、结果二元可判，单用 code 检查就够，不必上 LLM judge。
tradeoff: 自动化评分的速度与规模 vs 人工评分的准确与信任度

termDefinitions.meaning: 用另一个大模型按 rubric 给 agent 输出打分的评估方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LLM-as-judge uses another large language model to score an agent's output against a rubric.

termDefinitions.meaning: 描述评分维度和标准的打分细则。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A rubric is the set of criteria and standards used to score an output.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一批用来系统检验 agent 表现的任务样本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An eval set is a batch of task samples used to systematically check an agent's performance.

optionMeanings: 三种评分器按各自强项组合使用
只信任人工评分
只信任 LLM judge 单一评分器
认为评分标准不重要
optionMeanings_en: Combines all three graders, each used for its own strength.
Trusts only human grading and nothing else.
Trusts only a single LLM-judge grader.
Assumes the grading rubric doesn't really matter.
optionScenarioImpacts: 客观结果、主观维度、人工校准三层都覆盖到
人工成本高、难规模化，覆盖不了大量任务
LLM judge 本身非确定性，缺了客观核对和人工校准
评分不一致，无法真实反映 agent 是否变好
optionScenarioImpacts_en: It covers objective outcomes, subjective dimensions, and human calibration all at once.
Human review is expensive and doesn't scale to cover a large task volume.
LLM-judge is itself non-deterministic and lacks objective checks and human calibration.
Inconsistent scoring can't reliably show whether the agent is actually improving.
optionDirectness: 多步骤、既有客观又有主观维度时最贴切
只有任务量极小、结果高风险时单靠人工才现实
只有任务纯主观、允许一定噪声时才可能够用
几乎不成立，任何评估都需要明确标准
optionDirectness_en: Fits best for multi-step tasks that have both objective and subjective dimensions.
Realistic only when task volume is tiny and the stakes are very high.
May be enough only for purely subjective tasks that tolerate some noise.
Almost never valid — any evaluation needs a clear standard.

scenario: 你在给一个『帮用户填退款表单』的 agent 定评估指标，要求每次交互都必须成功，不能偶尔失败。
scenario_en: You're defining an eval metric for an agent that fills out refund forms, and every single interaction must succeed — occasional failure is not acceptable.
q: 面向用户、要求「每次都稳」的场景，该看哪个指标？
q_en: For a user-facing case that must succeed every single time, which metric should you use?
options: pass@k：k 次里至少 1 次成功
只看单次调用的成功率
只看平均响应延迟
pass^k：k 次必须全部成功
options_en: pass@k: at least 1 success out of k tries.
Just look at the single-call success rate.
Just look at average response latency.
pass^k: all k tries must succeed.
why: pass@k=1-(1-p)^k(至少1次成功)，pass^k=p^k(全部成功)。次次要稳就看 pass^k：p=99%时10步全稳概率仅约90%，逼你把单次成功率顶到99.9%+。
why_en: pass@k means at least one success in k tries; pass^k means all k succeed. User-facing reliability needs pass^k, since 99% per step compounds to ~90% over 10 steps.

termDefinitions.meaning: k 次尝试里至少成功一次的概率/指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: pass@k measures the probability that at least one of k attempts succeeds.

termDefinitions.meaning: k 次尝试全部成功的概率/指标，等于单次成功率的 k 次方。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: pass^k measures the probability that all k attempts succeed, equal to the single-run success rate raised to the k-th power.

optionMeanings: 选项主张：pass@k：k 次里至少 1 次成功。
选项主张：只看单次调用的成功率。
选项主张：只看平均响应延迟。
选项主张：pass^k：k 次必须全部成功。
optionDirectness: 只有题设改成这个方向时才适合。
只有这个绝对假设成立时才适合。
只有这个绝对假设成立时才适合。
适合本题给出的约束。
optionScenarioImpacts: 会让系统依赖「pass@k：k 次里至少 1 次成功」这个前提。
会让系统依赖「只看单次调用的成功率」这个前提。
会让系统依赖「只看平均响应延迟」这个前提。
会让方案围绕「pass^k：k 次必须全部成功」展开。
optionMeanings_en: pass@k: at least 1 success out of k tries.
Just look at the single-call success rate.
Just look at average response latency.
pass^k: all k tries must succeed.
optionDirectness_en: Only fits when the goal is to pass @k: at least 1 success out of k tries.
Only fits when this statement is true: just look at the single-call success rate.
Only fits when this statement is true: just look at average response latency.
Use when pass@k means at least one success in k tries.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: It commits the design to this assumption: pass@k: at least 1 success out of k tries.
It commits the design to this assumption: Just look at the single-call success rate.
It commits the design to this assumption: Just look at average response latency.
It commits the design to this path: pass^k: all k tries must succeed.
